claim: Novices with a code generator write training tasks faster and more correctly, but this does not show up reliably on later no-AI tests (immediate post-test null; retention d=0.28 and 0.41, not significant).
agent_test: Equal-token arm: scaffold-help vs plain; then test the same items without help (transfer) to see if gains persist.

claim: Learners who heavily delegate to AI score lower on later comprehension quizzes (d=0.738, 17% lower, 4.15 of 27 points, N=52) while task time is not significantly faster; high-scoring patterns involve asking for concepts. Lehmann 2025 (two pre-registered lab experiments) found no significant overall learning effect; usage pattern decides. Pattern clusters are small (n=2 to 7) and observational.
agent_test: Compare agent modes: delegate-code vs explain-then-code at equal tokens; score on held-out variants.

claim: AI help widens the gap: stronger or more experienced learners benefit, struggling students over-rely.
agent_test: Check whether scaffold gains are larger on easy items than on hard ones.
audit_note: Prather abstract (21 sessions, accelerators vs strugglers with illusion of competence) and Lehmann abstract (LLMs widen gap between low and high prior knowledge) match; evidence is a small qualitative study plus a partly exploratory split, and Lehmann found no overall effect.

claim: Experienced developers on familiar mature repos were 19% slower with early-2025 AI while forecasting 24% faster; a lab task with freelancers was 55.8% faster. Context (task, expertise) flips the sign.
agent_test: Report scaffold effect by task familiarity strata, not only the mean.

claim: LLM explanations of compiler error messages are usually comprehensible (67-100%) but the offered fix is correct only 33% of the time, and correct explanation ranges 11-83% by message.
agent_test: Have agent run the fix and recheck the error at equal tokens vs unverified fix.

claim: Prompt wording determines success: Copilot solved 47.6% verbatim, about 60% of the rest after rewording, and some conceptual problems failed every time.
agent_test: Test problem-restatement operator vs plain retry at equal tokens.
audit_note: Denny et al. full text verifies 79/166 (47.6%), 53 of 87 (60.9%) after rewording, 15 Conceptual problems failed every time; rewording was done manually by the authors; StudentEval (80 students, 1,749 prompts, 48 problems) supports prompt-wording sensitivity.

claim: Novices copy the task description straight into the generator (32% of 1646 prompts identical; 66% copied in another count) and use AI code unmodified in about half of tasks.
agent_test: Measure how often agent output is a copy of the prompt-derived draft.

claim: A large repository-data claim that language affects bugs shrinks under reanalysis: 36% false-positive bug labels, 27,450 duplicate commits (1.86%), many results no longer significant.
agent_test: Treat observational language-vs-quality claims as weak; prefer randomised comparisons.

claim: Roles of variables teaching gave no significant group differences on most exam parts; only roles vs animation differed on comprehension (N=44 analysed). Later reports are thinly documented.
agent_test: A/B a named-role state vocabulary in the scratchpad vs free notes at equal tokens.

claim: AI-assisted code had more security flaws and more false confidence (encryption 67% vs 79% correct; signing 3% vs 21% secure, N=47).
agent_test: Add a security-check pass and compare insecure-output rate at equal tokens.

claim: Agent-computer interface design matters: simple, compact, feedback-rich actions with guardrails gave 18.0% on SWE-bench Lite (GPT-4 Turbo); agent recovered 104 of 135 edit failures.
agent_test: Ablate guardrail messages in our tool interface at equal tokens.

claim: Guardrail-prompted tutors leak full solutions unless a separate filter is used; models are biased to give full solutions even when told not to.
agent_test: Check agent obeys 'do not give final answer' with and without an external check.
audit_note: CodeHelp text ('strongly biased towards providing a complete solution ... even when the prompt requests otherwise', separate code-removal prompt) verified; CodeAid paper reports 53% exact-solution leakage in Help Write Code and later pipeline changes; evidence is from 2023-era GPT-3.5-class models and the other CodeHelp rows are the same paper.

claim: Real-world novice errors follow a heavy-tailed distribution: Java 572 distinct messages, 127 seen once; Python 283, 42 once.
LLMs struggle on multiple-choice programming questions that include code (48.2% vs 77.9% text-only, text-davinci-003).
agent_test: Compare scaffolded vs plain on code-bearing items.

claim: In a Codex study of 240 generated CS1 exercises, 75.0% were rated sensible and 81.8% novel, but only 30.9% (51 of 165) of the exercises that had both a sample solution and automated tests had a sample solution that passed those tests.
agent_test: Execute generated tests against reference solutions as a gate.
audit_note: Sarsa et al. report 75.0% sensible and 81.8% novel, but 30.9% is 51 of 165 exercises that had both a sample solution and tests whose solution passed the tests (not 30.9% of all generated test sets); the second source (Denny review, same group) mislabels 30.9% as statement coverage and cannot be counted as independent.
claim_before_audit: Generated exercises: about 75-80% sensible and novel, but only 30.9% of generated test sets passed all checks.

claim: Enforcing the type system during decoding cuts compile errors by 75.3% (HumanEval) and 52.1% (MBPP) in TypeScript and raises functional correctness by only 3.5-5.5% relative; syntax-only constraining cuts 9% and 5%.
agent_test: Gate generated code with a compiler or type check inside the repair loop; compare to no gate at equal tokens.

claim: Static typing of the target language has no overall effect on Codex pass@1 across 19 languages (p=0.34 and p=0.23); removing Python annotations has no effect (p=0.23); weakening TypeScript types to Any costs 2.5% (p<0.001). Only 2022 models tested.
agent_test: Rerun on a 2025-26 model before relying on it.

claim: Interface details matter for agents: in SWE-agent ablations, removing the edit action cost 7.7 points, removing linting 3.0, iterative search 6.0 below summarized search; viewer 100 lines beat 30 or full file. Equal-token comparison was not done.
agent_test: Repeat ablation with a fixed token budget.
